name: Reed Hastings
current_role: Co-founder of Netflix (left board in 2026 after serving as chairman); majority owner of Powder Mountain ski resort, Utah
profile: Co-founded Netflix in 1997 after selling his first company, Pure Software, and turned it from DVD-by-mail into the dominant streaming service. Stepped down as co-CEO in 2023, became executive chairman, and in April 2026 said he would leave Netflix's board. Now focused on Powder Mountain (bought control in 2023) and education philanthropy; lifetime giving above $2bn.
interesting_fact: Before college he deferred Bowdoin for a year to keep selling Rainbow vacuum cleaners door to door, a summer job he said he liked; he then taught math in the Peace Corps in Swaziland.
deep_cut_fact: He has put more than $100m of his own capital into Powder Mountain, Utah, and in 2026 announced a further $157m for its private Powder Haven area, adding two new lifts for the 2026-27 season. The resort also has an outdoor art museum.
notes: Leaving Netflix's board as of summer 2026, so Powder Mountain is the likelier route. The Netflix newsroom lists only regional press contacts, so none is a direct line to him. Ties to the podcast topics: education philanthropy and real estate/resort development.

name: Uma Devi Prasad
current_role: Listed by Hurun (2025-26) as a holder of Aristo Pharmaceuticals wealth; no executive role found
profile: Hurun links her to Aristo Pharmaceuticals, the Mumbai-based drugmaker founded in 1971 by Mahendra Prasad, a seven-term Rajya Sabha MP who died in December 2021. Public records name an Uma Devi in disputes over his estate. I could not confirm her role at the company or any public profile.
notes: Very private, with almost no public profile. Her link to Aristo is tied up in ongoing estate litigation over Mahendra Prasad's assets, so this is a sensitive family matter: avoid. The only contact is the company's general email. Low priority.

name: Lawrence Stroll
current_role: Executive Chairman and controlling shareholder, Aston Martin Lagonda; owner of the Aston Martin Aramco F1 team
profile: Montreal-born fashion investor who, with Silas Chou, built Tommy Hilfiger and then Michael Kors into global brands and cashed out after Kors' 2011 IPO. Bought the Force India F1 team in 2018, led a 2020 rescue investment in Aston Martin, and now runs both the carmaker and its F1 team (with Adrian Newey on board).
interesting_fact: He collects vintage Ferraris and paid a then-record $27.5m for a 1967 Ferrari 275 GTB/4*S N.A.R.T. Spider in 2013.
deep_cut_fact: He owned Quebec's historic Circuit Mont-Tremblant, a former Canadian Grand Prix venue, from 2000 until selling it in 2022. In 2021 he listed it for sale, then took it off the market.
notes: Gives few interviews. The best route is the Aston Martin corporate or F1 team press office (media.astonmartin.com).
